title: A cohomology Tor interval bounds the Tor interval of a bounded complex
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_X))$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $a\leq b$ and $c\leq d$ be integers. Suppose $H^q(K)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$ and, for every $q\in[a,b]$, the module $H^q(K)$ in degree zero has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$ [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. Then $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a+c,b+d]$. No constructibility assumption on its cohomology is required.

source.place: Complexes, truncation induction with a general common cohomology Tor interval

proof.text: Let C be the actual category of internal Λ_X-module sheaves in the statement. Let Q be Tor amplitude in I=[a+c,b+d]. For every q let P_q(M) mean a≤q≤b and Tor amplitude [c,d] for M in degree zero. Isomorphism invariance of Tor amplitude and of the single functor makes every P_q replete. Since a≤b and c≤d, I is ordered.

source.place: Complexes, truncation induction with a general common cohomology Tor interval

proof.text: For a zero derived object M and any test module N, the additive relative derived tensor functor F_N=(-)⊗ᴸN[0] sends M to zero. Every cohomology of F_N(M) is zero, so Q(M). For a distinguished triangle, the extension clause of constantModelConstructibleFiniteTor_wellDefined gives Q for its middle object from Q on its outer objects, with the common interval I.

source.place: Complexes, truncation induction with a general common cohomology Tor interval

proof.text: For P_q(M), use the existing K-flat derived tensor shift comparison F_N(M[0][-q])≅F_N(M[0])[-q]. The standard t-structure shift formula moves the bounds [c,d] to [c-(-q),d-(-q)]=[q+c,q+d]. Since a≤q≤b this interval lies in I. Transport the enlarged amplitude through the existing single-functor isomorphism M[0][-q]≅M[q], where the latter denotes placement in degree q. This proves Q(single_q M), including negative q. The tensor is the same relative internal-module tensor used in torAmplitudeIn, with no change of coefficient category.

source.place: Complexes, truncation induction with a general common cohomology Tor interval

proof.text: The vanishing hypothesis gives K.IsGE a and K.IsLE b by the standard cohomological characterizations. Apply the already proved degreewise dévissage theorem with Q and P_q above, n=(b-a+1).toNat and lower bound a. Since a≤b, a+n-1=b. The preceding steps supply zero, extension, repleteness and degreewise single-object conditions; hH supplies P_q(H^q(K)) throughout the induction interval. The conclusion is exactly Tor amplitude [a+c,b+d] for K. The dévissage theorem uses the same finite truncation induction as the blueprint, rather than reconstructing it in this module.
